newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the Commission will start its weekly meeting in Strasbourg at 1500/1300 GMT on Tuesday after which Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti will hold a news conference on a green paper on supplementary pensions in Strasbourg at 1630/1430 GMT.

The Commission's daily news briefing on Wednesday will start at 1145/0945 because Commission President Jacques Santer will hold a news conference in Strasbourg at 1200/1000 GMT on next week's European Council in Amsterdam.
Both news conferences will be relayed to Brussels.
Vale de Almeida said the Commission's Business and Consumer Survey in May showed that confidence was rising in all member states except Denmark and Italy.

Spokesman Jochen Kubosch said that the European Court of Justice had ruled in favour of the European Parliament and annulled Council Regulation 2317/95 specifying non-EU countries whose nationals must have visas when crossing the external borders of EU member states. But it will remain in force until the Council has adopted a new regulation to deal with the issue.
In response to a question, spokesman Peter Guilford said that the EU will initial a Mutual Recognition Agreement with the United States in the next few days.

Spokesman Patrick Child answered numerous questions on the timetable of economic and monetary union (EMU) after France said on Monday it needed more time to study the stability pact, a key element of EMU.
The Commission was working on a resolution for next week's summit in Amsterdam that would deal with the coordination of economic policies, especially regarding growth and employment, he said.

There was no crisis, he stressed, adding that the clear message from a large majority of member states at Monday's ECOFIN meeting was to keep to the timetable set at the EU Dublin Council and that the EMU text should be published by July 1, 1997.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/504: Humanitarian Aid - Cambodia, Burkina Faso, Chad, Guinea Bissau.
- IP/97/505: European Commission clears acquisition of AST by Samsung but considers imposing a fine for late filing.
- Business and Consumer Surveys: First Results May 1997 - No.5
